subject: physics
question_text: What is resonance? Give one example.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: When a body is driven by a periodic force whose
frequency is equal to the natural frequency of
the body, it oscillates with a very large
steps.why: Resonance is a special case of forced oscillation, not a separate kind of motion.
common_mistakes: Defining it as any large oscillation, without the frequency condition.

recall.must_convey: That resonance is a very large amplitude when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.

steps.memory_tip: Tuning a radio is resonance: the circuit oscillates strongly at one frequency only.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The frequency condition has to sit inside the definition sentence.

steps.label: Condition and example
lines: Example: pushing a swing in time with its own
swinging makes it rise higher and higher, while
pushing at any other rate does very little.
steps.why: Each push arrives exactly when it helps, so the energy fed in adds up instead of partly cancelling.
common_mistakes: Giving an example where the two frequencies are unrelated.

recall.must_convey: That the condition is equal frequencies, as when a swing is pushed in time with its own swinging.

steps.memory_tip: A swing is pushed once per swing, not once per second. The rate has to match the swing.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The condition and the example both belong to this mark.

insider_note: The second mark holds both the condition and the example, and a definition without the frequency condition earns nothing.
